summary: AgriOrbit is a crop-rotation decision-support web app that helps farmers compare multi-season rotation plans using NASA Earth observations, soil data and their own priorities. A farmer sets up a farm and its current rotation. AgriOrbit then pulls NASA POWER climate data, SoilGrids estimates and an uploaded Soil Health Card report. It screens 16 crops for soil pH, salinity, temperature, water and season-length limits, and ranks feasible rotations by net income, irrigation need, soil organic carbon change and pest-break benefit, with legume nitrogen fixation counted as a plan benefit. Farmers can adopt a plan, monitor it with NASA GIBS satellite layers, and ask an AI agronomist (English or Malayalam) whose answers are limited to computed project facts. Every data source is labelled live, cached, fixture or unavailable, so farmers see what the evidence is.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Farmers face shifting temperatures, uneven rainfall, water shortages and declining soil health, which makes it hard to choose rotations that protect soil, save water and still earn income. Evidence is scattered across weather sources, maps and lab reports, and goals such as income, water use and soil benefit pull in different directions.

WHAT AGRIORBIT DOES

AgriOrbit brings planning, monitoring and advice into one application:

- Set up a farm: location, growing zone, farm boundary and the existing "baseline" rotation, which is the reference for every proposed plan.

- Review data: NASA POWER agroclimatology (rainfall, temperature, radiation, humidity, wind) and SoilGrids soil estimates. Farmers can also upload a Soil Health Card (PDF or CSV). Values are shown in an editable preview before saving and are marked measured, estimated, missing or unsupported. Missing values are never invented.

- Check crops: each of 16 crops is labelled eligible, excluded (with a reason: soil pH, salinity, temperature, water, duration or region), not evaluated, or lacking data.

- Compare plans: a constrained multi-objective Pareto optimizer scores each plan on net income, irrigation required, change in soil organic carbon and pest-break score. Farmers can adjust objective weights. Constraints include a maximum number of cover crops, a minimum number of cash-crop seasons and a minimum income floor. Planning horizons (for example 1 year with 3 seasons, or 3 years with 1 season each) are matched to the climate zone.

- Adopt and monitor: NASA GIBS layers (NDVI, rainfall, root-zone soil moisture, land surface temperature), a 30-day water balance, an activity log, baseline-drift detection and plan-versus-baseline reports. The app works offline as a PWA.

- Ask the AI agronomist: answers in English and Malayalam are restricted to computed project facts, carry verified citation tags, and list missing evidence when data is thin.

HOW IT WORKS

Water physics uses FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference evapotranspiration (ET0), crop water demand ETc = Kc x ET0, and a water balance of rainfall minus ET0. Drought (-30% rain), monsoon flood (+35% rain) and heat (+2.5 C) runs are labelled historical sensitivity stress tests, not forecasts. Plans are ranked with a weighted composite of normalized objectives; infeasible plans stay at rank 0.

SCIENTIFIC HONESTY

Each data source reports its status (live, cached, fixture or unavailable), version, resolution and last update, and fixtures are never presented as live. NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 future projections are planned but not yet integrated. No physical sensors are connected, and the built-in test farms (Thrissur, Palakkad, Wayanad, Iowa, Fresno) are internal software checks, not field trials. AgriOrbit supports review of trade-offs; it does not replace local agronomic expertise or guarantee yield.

BENEFITS AND GOALS

Farmers get one transparent place to explore rotations that balance income, water and soil health under changing conditions, using free and open NASA data. Next steps: integrate CMIP6 climate projections, extend crop and regional coverage, and validate assumptions with agronomists and field data.

TOOLS

React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, Express (Node.js), Leaflet, Recharts, i18next (English/Malayalam), pdfjs-dist, TanStack Query, vite-plugin-pwa, Google Gemini API (@google/genai), hosted on Render.
